The deer population needs to be culled if they are damaging the balsam fir forest's reproduction. No tree lives forever and once a species is gone, it is gone. As these deer are isolated from other populations, I'm assuming that they haven't been exposed to the wasting and other diseases that have been found among mainland herds. Thus the meat is safe to preserve and eat. 
The other option is to fence off large tracts to allow fir seedlings to sprout and grow big enough to survive the deer.
